title: AC languages have polynomial circuit size
statement: If a language over Boolean strings is recognized by a well-formed family of Boolean circuits of polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth, then there are natural numbers $a$ and $k$ such that the language is recognized by a family of circuits with at most two inputs per gate whose size on inputs of length $n$ is at most $a(n+1)^k$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language over Boolean strings
$L$ has a well-formed circuit family of polynomial size
That family has polylogarithmic depth for some natural-number exponent
